newsitem.title: FRANCE: Suspected Islamists kill 11 more in Algeria.
newsitem.headline: Suspected Islamists kill 11 more in Algeria.

text.p: Suspected Moslem fundamentalists killed 11 people overnight in Medea province, south of Algiers, Algerian security forces said on Thursday.

News of the killings, in a statement carried by the official Algerian news agency APS, brought to eight the number of attacks reported on civilians in the past two weeks in which nearly 90 people have died.
The security forces said the 11 were "assassinated in a cowardly way" -- the term used by security officials for killings by Moslem fundamentalists, usually with victims having their throats cut.
They said the killings took place in Ain-Dema, in Medea province, whose capital lies some 50 km (30 miles) south of Algiers.

On Wednesday, security forces reported the slaughter of 12 Algerians, including four women and three children, in the tiny community of Douar Ben-Salah, near the scene one week earlier of the massacre of 32 people in another village.
Algerian newspapers said on Thursday, before news of the latest killing broke, that 76 people had been killed in mass assassinations blamed on Moslem fundamentalists.

The rise in attacks on civilians, unrelated to members of the security forces and apparently not involved in the five-year-old conflict, started shortly after the authorities announced a referendum would be held on November 28 to change the constitution.
One of the main changes will be to ban political parties based on religion.
An estimated 50,000 people have been killed in Algeria's violence since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists took a huge lead.
Algerian legal opposition parties put the death toll at 70,000-100,000 while the outlawed Islamic Salvation Front says 120,000 people have died.
